test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 16 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: One pipe can fill a tank in 8 minutes, while another pipe can empty the completely filled tank in 16 minutes. If both the pipes are opened together when the tank is empty, how many minutes will it take to fill one-fourth of the tank?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net part filled by both pipes in 1 minute = (1/8) − (1/16) = 1/16

This means the completely empty tank will be filled in 16 minutes.

Time taken to fill 1/4th of the tank = 16 × (1/4) = 4 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 4 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by filling pipe (Pipe A) = 8 minutes

Time taken by emptying pipe (Pipe B) = 16 minutes

Let total capacity of the tank be the LCM of 8 and 16.

 
 

 **Pipe**
 **Minutes**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 Pipe A (Fill)
 8
 16
 +2
 
 

 Pipe B (Empty)
 16
 −1
 
 

⇒ Combined efficiency of both pipes = (+2) + (−1) = +1 unit/min

⇒ We need to fill one-fourth of the tank.

⇒ Target capacity = 1/4 × Total Work = 1/4 × 16 = 4 units

⇒ Time required = Target capacity ÷ Combined efficiency

⇒ Time required = 4 ÷ 1 = 4 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 4 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inlet and Outlet Pipes

An inlet pipe fills the tank (positive work), while an outlet pipe empties it (negative work). The net efficiency is the algebraic sum of their individual efficiencies.

Combined Rate Formula

If pipe A fills in x hours and pipe B empties in y hours (where y > x), the net part filled in 1 hour is (1/x − 1/y). The total time to fill the tank is xy ÷ (y − x).

Partial Work

Time required for a partial job = (Fraction of work × Total Capacity) ÷ Net Efficiency.
